channel.title: 전체기사 : 함께하는 교육 : 뉴스 : 한겨레 뉴스 - 인터넷한겨레 (Bilingual Full Text)

item.title: "We will make AI the foundation for all disciplines and solving urban problems" (“AI를 모든 학문과 도시 문제 해결의 기반으로 삼겠다”)
item.description:
Interview with Won Yong-geol, President of the University of Seoul (원용걸 서울시립대학교 총장 인터뷰)

In an era of upheaval where artificial intelligence (AI) and cutting-edge technology are reshaping the order of society as a whole, the role of universities is also facing fundamental questions. Where should education and research be headed, and what kind of talent should universities cultivate? Won Yong-geol, President of the University of Seoul, now in his fourth year in office, offered a clear direction to these questions. (인공지능(AI)과 첨단 기술이 사회 전반의 질서를 재편하는 격변의 시대, 대학의 역할 역시 근본적인 질문에 직면하고 있다. 교육과 연구는 어디로 향해야 하며, 대학은 어떤 인재를 길러내야 하는가. 총장 취임 4년차에 접어든 서울시립대학교 원용걸 총장은 이 질문에 대해 분명한 방향을 제시했다.)

While preserving the identity of a public university, he has led a shift toward an education and research system that integrates AI based on urban science. As chairman of the Seoul Presidents' Forum, he has also dedicated efforts to cooperation and solidarity in higher education across Seoul. Now that his term as chairman of the Seoul Presidents' Forum is nearing its end, we met with President Won to hear about the direction universities should take in a rapidly changing era, his philosophy on talent development, and the next steps the University of Seoul is preparing. (공립대학의 정체성을 지키는 한편, 도시과학을 기반으로 인공지능과 융합한 교육·연구 체계로의 전환을 이끌어 온 그는 서울총장포럼 회장으로서 서울 고등교육 전반의 협력과 연대에도 힘을 쏟아왔다. 서울총장포럼 회장 임기가 마무리 국면에 접어든 지금, 원 총장을 만나 급변하는 시대에 대학이 나아가야 할 방향과 인재 양성 철학, 그리고 서울시립대가 준비하는 다음 단계를 들어봤다.)

– What kind of talent does the ‘PSG talent profile’ you emphasize refer to? (–총장님이 강조한 ‘PSG 인재상’은 어떤 인재를 말하나.)

“The advancement of AI and digital technology is changing not only industrial structures but also the way humans relate to society. In times like these, I believe universities must present standards that consider people and society as much as technological competitiveness. The talent profile I have proposed is the PSG talent: individuals equipped with a balanced blend of Personal Capacity, Social Capacity, and Global Capacity. Personal capacity includes specialized knowledge, problem-solving skills, and lifelong learning ability. Social capacity is a sense of responsibility and empathy to give back to society the benefits of education received. Global capacity is an attitude of challenging the global stage based on an understanding of other cultures and values. (“인공지능과 디지털 기술의 발전은 산업 구조뿐 아니라 인간이 사회와 관계를 맺는 방식까지 바꾸고 있다. 이런 시대일수록 대학은 기술 경쟁력 못지않게 사람과 사회를 함께 생각할 수 있는 기준을 제시해야 한다고 본다. 내가 제시해온 인재상은 PSG 인재, 즉 개인 역량(Personal Capacity), 사회적 역량(Social Capacity), 글로벌 역량(Global Capacity)을 균형 있게 갖춘 인재다. 개인 역량은 전공 지식과 문제 해결 능력, 그리고 평생 학습 역량을 포함한다. 사회적 역량은 자신이 받은 교육 혜택을 사회에 환원하려는 책임 의식과 공감 능력이다. 글로벌 역량은 다른 문화와 가치에 대한 이해를 바탕으로 세계 무대에 도전하는 태도다.)

This talent profile is implemented in the educational field so that students experience it firsthand. The Global Volunteer Group is a representative example of fostering social and global capacities together. Last January, it conducted education and cultural exchange activities for elementary and middle school students in the Thai Nguyen region, Vietnam. Additionally, through the student-led global career exploration program ‘UOS Career Expedition,’ we support students in visiting universities and companies in North America and Europe to design their own career paths.” (이러한 인재상은 교육 현장에서 학생들이 직접 경험하도록 구현하고 있다. 글로벌봉사단은 사회적·글로벌 역량을 함께 기르는 대표적 사례로, 지난 1월 베트남 타이응우옌 지역에서 초·중학생을 대상으로 교육과 문화 교류 활동을 진행했다. 또한 학생 주도형 글로벌 진로 탐색 프로그램인 ‘UOS커리어원정대’를 통해 학생들이 북미와 유럽 현지에서 대학과 기업을 탐방하며 스스로 진로를 설계하도록 지원하고 있다.”)

– The student-centered academic system reform stands out. (–학생 중심 학사제도 개편이 눈에 띈다.)

“We are reforming the system to allow students to flexibly design their majors and career paths, such as making AI basic courses mandatory for all students, establishing new AI·SW convergence majors for non-majors, operating micro-degrees and intensive course systems. Through the ‘Major Design and Convergence Support Center,’ we provide step-by-step counseling from admission to graduation. A structure where students can choose and design for themselves is important.” (“전교생 AI 기초 교과목 필수화, 비전공자 대상 AI·SW 융합전공 신설, 마이크로 디그리와 집중이수제 운영 등 학생들이 전공과 진로를 유연하게 설계할 수 있도록 제도를 바꾸고 있다. ‘전공설계융합지원센터’를 통해 입학부터 졸업까지 단계별 상담도 제공한다. 학생이 스스로 선택하고 설계할 수 있는 구조가 중요하다.”)

– What is the biggest change for nurturing talent in cutting-edge fields? (–첨단 분야 인재 양성을 위한 가장 큰 변화는 무엇인가.)

“The biggest change is that we are building an environment where AI is not confined to specific majors but is actually utilized across education, research, and administration. As part of this, after a trial run in December 2025, we fully launched the generative AI information service ‘AIChat’ in January 2026. It is designed so that all students, faculty, and staff can safely and responsibly use generative AI based on an integrated LLM (Large Language Model). This coming March, the AI Convergence College will be launched, integrating the Department of Computer Science, the Department of Artificial Intelligence, and the Division of Advanced Convergence. This is not a simple organizational restructuring but a paradigm shift in education to make AI the foundation for all disciplines and solving urban problems. The AI Convergence College will collaborate organically with the ‘AI·SW Convergence Education Institute,’ which is the dedicated department for the ‘Software-Centered University Project,’ to advance the curriculum, strengthen practical training and industry-academia linkages, and function as a hub college for cultivating practical, cutting-edge convergence talent required by future society.” (“가장 큰 변화는 인공지능을 특정 전공에 국한하지 않고 교육·연구·행정 전반에서 실제로 활용하는 환경을 구축하고 있다는 점이다. 그 일환으로 2025년 12월 시범 운영을 거쳐 2026년 1월부터 생성형 AI 정보서비스 ‘AIChat’을 본격 도입했다. 학생과 교수, 직원 모두가 통합 LLM(대규모 언어모델) 기반 생성형 AI를 안전하고 책임감 있게 활용할 수 있도록 설계했다. 오는 3월에는 컴퓨터과학부, 인공지능학과, 첨단융합학부를 통합한 인공지능융합대학이 출범한다. 이는 단순한 조직 개편이 아니라, AI를 모든 학문과 도시 문제 해결의 기반으로 삼겠다는 교육 패러다임의 전환이다. 인공지능융합대학은 ‘SW중심대학 사업’ 전담 부서인 ‘AI·SW융합교육원’과 유기적으로 협력해, 교육과정 고도화와 실습·산학 연계를 강화하고, 미래 사회가 요구하는 실용적·첨단 융합인재 양성의 거점 단과대학으로 기능할 예정이다.”)

– What role does the University of Seoul, as a public university, aim to play? (–공립대학으로써 서울시립대가 지향하는 역할은 무엇인가.)

“The University of Seoul is a public university operated with the support and trust of Seoul. This is both a source of pride and a responsibility. I believe that the outcomes of education and research should not remain within the university but should spread to the lives of citizens and the public sphere. This awareness is clearly evident in our collaboration on AI education with public schools. Recently, we signed an AI education agreement with the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education and jointly operated a job training program on GPU-based deep learning (CNN) modeling for information teachers in middle and high schools. This is a case of directly connecting the university’s research infrastructure and expertise to the public education field. A public university should not stop at accumulating knowledge but also play a role in elevating the overall educational capacity of society.” (“서울시립대는 서울의 지원과 신뢰 속에서 운영되는 공립대학이다. 이는 자부심이자 동시에 책임이다. 교육과 연구의 성과가 학교 안에 머무르지 않고 시민의 삶과 공공 영역으로 확산돼야 한다고 생각한다. 이런 인식은 공교육과의 AI 교육 협력에서도 분명히 나타난다. 최근 서울시교육청과 AI 교육 협약을 체결하고, 중·고등학교 정보교사를 대상으로 GPU 활용 딥러닝(CNN) 모델링 직무연수를 공동 운영했다. 대학의 연구 인프라와 전문성을 공교육 현장과 직접 연결한 사례다. 공립대학은 지식을 축적하는 데서 그치지 않고, 사회 전체의 교육 역량을 함께 끌어올리는 역할을 해야 한다.”)

– Your activities as the 11th-term chairman of the Seoul Presidents' Forum have also drawn attention. (–서울총장포럼 제11기 회장으로서의 활동도 주목받았다.)

“The Seoul Presidents' Forum is a consultative body where the presidents of 39 universities in Seoul participate to discuss current issues in higher education and seek cooperative measures. As chairman, my primary focus was on creating a cooperative structure that shares resources and capabilities beyond inter-university competition. (“서울총장포럼은 서울 소재 39개 대학 총장이 참여해 고등교육의 현안을 논의하고 협력 방안을 모색하는 협의체다. 회장으로서 가장 중점을 둔 부분은 대학 간 경쟁을 넘어 자원과 역량을 공유하는 협력 구조를 만드는 것이었다.)

In the forum, we have continued discussions centered on demand-driven cooperation models, such as a cloud-based shared university platform, credit exchanges, joint curricula, and Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs). Particularly, 2025 was the first year the Regional Innovation-Oriented University Support System (RISE) project was fully implemented, and we collectively contemplated structures where universities' education and research capabilities could spread to regions and industries. (포럼에서는 클라우드 기반 공유대학 플랫폼, 학점 교류, 연합 교육과정, 온라인 공개강좌(MOOC) 등 수요자 중심 협력 모델을 중심으로 논의를 이어왔다. 특히 2025년은 지역혁신중심 대학지원체계(RISE) 사업이 본격 시행되는 첫 해로, 대학의 교육·연구 역량이 지역과 산업으로 확산될 수 있는 구조를 함께 고민했다.)

These discussions materialized through a recent RISE industry-academia cooperation outcome-sharing event. It confirmed that convergence and integrated technologies in AI, robotics, and mobility are directly connecting with companies, and that industry-academia cooperation is evolving into a practical cooperative structure linking research–technology–commercialization.” (이러한 논의는 최근 열린 RISE 산학협력 성과 공유 행사를 통해 구체화됐다. AI·로봇·모빌리티 등 융·복합 기술이 기업과 직접 연결되며, 산학협력이 연구–기술–사업화로 이어지는 실질적 협력 구조로 진화하고 있음을 확인했다.”)

– What areas do you particularly want to focus on in university management going forward? (–앞으로 대학 운영에서 특히 집중하고 싶은 부분은.)

“I want to focus on ensuring that the innovations in education, research, and entrepreneurship we have driven so far become established as tangible outcomes and spread. Over the past four years, the Campus Town project office supported 215 startup teams, achieving results of 31.8 billion won in sales, 14.6 billion won in investment attraction, and the creation of 845 jobs. Based on this, we plan to fully operate the ‘Seoul Impact 2.0’ strategy and expand AI-based urban problem-solving startups in connection with the Seoul RISE project. We also plan to support young people to participate as agents of urban problem-solving through programs like the ‘SEOUL:ution Hackathon.’ A university is not a place that provides answers but a space that helps ask questions and find answers independently. As a public university, we will establish ourselves as a university that creates urban innovation and social value befitting the AI era together.” (“지금까지 추진해온 교육·연구·창업 혁신이 실제 성과로 정착되고 확산되는 데 집중하고 싶다. 최근 4년간 캠퍼스타운 사업단은 215개 창업팀을 지원해 매출 318억원, 투자 유치 146억원, 일자리 845명 창출이라는 성과를 거뒀다. 이를 바탕으로 ‘Seoul Impact 2.0’ 전략을 본격 가동하고, 서울 RISE 사업과 연계해 AI 기반 도시 문제 해결형 창업을 확장할 계획이다. 또 ‘SEOUL:ution 해커톤’과 같은 프로그램을 통해 청년들이 도시 문제 해결의 주체로 참여하도록 지원할 예정이다. 대학은 정답을 주는 곳이 아니라 질문을 던지고 스스로 답을 찾도록 돕는 공간이다. 공립대학으로써 AI 시대에 걸맞은 도시 혁신과 사회적 가치를 함께 만들어가는 대학으로 자리 잡아 나가겠다.”)

This year, the University of Seoul established the AI Convergence College to foster talent in cutting-edge fields and strengthen convergence and integrated education and research capabilities to meet the demands of the 4th industrial revolution, including AI. By transferring existing AI-related departments from the College of Engineering—such as the Department of Computer Science and the Department of Artificial Intelligence—and the Division of Advanced Convergence from the College of Liberal Arts and Convergence, which are advanced departments, the University of Seoul consolidated previously scattered advanced departments like AI and semiconductors into the new AI Convergence College. For the 2026 academic year, a total of 128 students were recruited. The AI Convergence College consists of the Department of Computer Science, the Department of Artificial Intelligence, and the Division of Advanced Convergence (with majors in Advanced AI, Intelligent Semiconductors, and Convergence Bio-Health). (서울시립대는 올해 AI 등 4차 산업 수요에 부응하기 위한 첨단 분야 인재육성 및 융·복합 교육·연구 역량을 강화하기 위해 인공지능융합대학을 설립했다. 기존 공과대학의 AI 관련 학과인 컴퓨터과학부, 인공지능학과와 자유융합대학의 첨단학과인 첨단융합학부를 인공지능융합대학으로 이관하는 등 각 단과대학에 흩어져 있던 AI, 반도체 등 첨단 관련 학부·과를 통합해 인공지능융합대학을 신설하고 2026학년도에 총 128명을 모집했다. 인공지능융합대학은 컴퓨터과학부, 인공지능학과, 첨단융합학부(첨단인공지능·지능형반도체·융합바이오헬스 전공)로 학부·과가 구성된다.)

Additionally, the AI Convergence College shares the common AI foundational courses it developed and jointly operates 14 AI convergence major roadmaps for non-majors. Through academic systems like double majors, minors, and micro-degrees, students can build AI capabilities regardless of their primary major. Using infrastructure from SW-centered universities, such as supercomputer clusters, AI startup education within the Campus Town initiative is also implemented. (또한 인공지능융합대학에서 개발한 AI 공통 기초 교과목을 공유하며 비전공생을 위한 14개 AI 융합전공 로드맵을 공동 운영, 복수전공·부전공·마이크로디그리 등 학사 제도를 통해 전공과 상관없이 AI 역량을 쌓을 수 있도록 지원한다. 슈퍼컴퓨터 클러스터 등 SW 중심 대학의 인프라를 활용해 캠퍼스타운의 AI 창업 교육도 실행한다.)

Starting with this year's freshmen, AI·SW basic education has been made mandatory for all students, with new required liberal arts courses established and curricula operated by academic track. Notably, among the 23 comprehensive majors in the Division of Convergence Innovation, the ‘Urban Analytics Convergence Major’ combines urban science with AI technology, securing a competitive edge that differentiates it from other universities. (올해 신입생부터 전교생을 대상으로 AI·SW 기초교육을 의무화해 교양필수 교과목을 신설하고 계열별 교육과정을 운영한다. 특히 융합전공학부의 23개 통섭전공 가운데 ‘도시애널리틱스융합전공’은 도시과학과 AI 기술을 결합한 교육과정으로, 타 대학과 차별화된 경쟁력을 확보했다.)

World-class research infrastructure, such as the ‘Supercomputer,’ ‘UOS Semiconductor Fab,’ the Smart Mobility Lounge, and a high-performance Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM), provides a foundation for students to grow while combining classes, practical training, and research. Along with recruiting new faculty in cutting-edge fields and expanding convergence research projects, the university is creating a virtuous cycle of education and research by developing Seoul-style regional innovation models through the Seoul RISE project. (‘슈퍼컴퓨터’ ‘UOS 반도체 Fab’, 스마트 모빌리티 라운지, 고성능 투과전자현미경(TEM) 등 세계적 수준의 연구 인프라는 학생들이 수업과 실습, 연구를 병행하며 성장할 수 있는 토대가 되고 있다. 여기에 첨단 분야 신임 교수 영입, 융합형 연구 프로젝트 확대와 더불어 서울 RISE 사업을 통해 서울형 지역혁신 모델 개발을 통해 교육과 연구가 선순환하는 구조를 만들어가고 있다.)

These efforts have led to the operation of multi-major and modular curriculum systems and the establishment of an integrated support system for career, academics, and employment based on student growth cycles (AMAZE), practically implementing student-centered educational innovation. The strengthening of foundational disciplines, expansion of convergence education, and improvement of the academic system are results of the consistent educational innovation pursued by the University of Seoul. Ultimately, the goal is to cultivate practical convergence talent equipped with both the ability to solve future urban problems and advanced AI application capabilities. (이러한 노력은 다전공·모듈형 교육과정 운영, 학생 성장 주기에 기반한 진로·학업·취업 통합지원 시스템(AMAZE) 구축 등으로 이어지며, 학생 중심 교육혁신을 실질적으로 구현해 왔다. 기초학문 강화와 융복합 교육 확대, 학사제도 개선은 서울시립대가 일관되게 추진해 온 교육혁신의 결과다. 궁극적으로는 미래 도시 문제 해결 능력과 첨단 AI 활용 역량을 함께 갖춘 실용적 융합인재를 길러내는 것을 목표로 한다.)

By Jeong Hee-kyung, Reporter ahyun04@hani.co.kr, Photo provided by the University of Seoul (정희경 기자 ahyun04@hani.co.kr, 사진 서울시립대 제공)

item.title: A Girl from the 'Space Boys' Unit Draws Tomorrow for Children and the Earth in the Classroom (‘우주소년단’ 소녀, 교단에서 아이들과 지구의 내일을 그리다)
item.description:
Kim Eun-ji | Teacher at Wirye Elementary School, Hanam, Gyeonggi Province & Member of the Global Citizenship Education Research Institute (김은지 | 경기 하남 위례초 교사·세계시민교육연구소 회원)

In elementary school, the youth group I chose was the 'Space Boys' Unit. It seemed impressive how it explored science without gender distinction and dreamed of humanity's peace and future. On the day of the inauguration ceremony, standing shoulder to shoulder with male students in the uniform, a girl thought, 'It would have been better if it were called the Space Boys and Girls Unit or Space Youth Unit.' Now, two decades later, she has become an elementary school teacher and dreams of a sustainable world. <<> The period when I began to seriously pursue the dream of 'a life of action for a sustainable Earth' started in the second semester of 2025, when I returned to work as a science specialist teacher. Drawing on my experiences from participating in a Climate Fresk workshop and training programs for resource circulation and climate change science instructors during my leave, I operated '5-minute environmental education' within science classes and an 'environmental autonomous club.' <<> When I shared experiences like 'tree planting on a warming Arbor Day,' 'ocean plogging,' and 'No-Plastic Run' with photos, the children's eyes sparkled from the very first session. The 5-minute environmental education culminated in a 'Junior Climate Fresk' activity at the end of the semester. The co-facilitators who joined as educational volunteers marveled at the children's deep understanding and sensitivity toward the environment. <<> The environmental autonomous club 'Green Keeper,' consisting of 20 students from grades 5 to 6, held two periods of activities every Friday. From the club name contest onward, the students were proactive, participating in the 'Gyeonggi Province Climate Volunteer Corps-Kibongi' activities and ocean plogging held at Bangameori Beach. Eunsang, a participant, shared, "It was hot, but I felt proud picking up trash with the mindset of protecting the Earth!" <<> The '3rd Save the Earth Festival' held at Gwanghwamun Square in Seoul was the students' most memorable experience. Having built foundational knowledge, including carbon neutrality, through a visit from the 'Hanam City Environmental Education Center,' they even enjoyed the joy of having an elementary school student become the last survivor in the 'Environmental Golden Bell' competition involving elementary, middle, and high school students. <<> The students' experiences of the wider world outside school led to donations. They contributed over half of the school prize money to Greenpeace (environment), the UN Refugee Agency (human rights), and the Animal Rights Action KARA (animal rights). <<> Green Keeper members learned correct methods for separating aseptic packs and paper packs through 'Forest & Share's Paper Pack Resource Circulation Education.' In a class with vegan author Jo Min-ju, they made vegan sandwiches and experienced dietary habits for the planet. Using materials and tools provided by 'Uja School (A Healthy School Free from Hazardous Substances),' they identified hazardous substances around us and learned lifestyle rules to protect their health and the Earth's. <<> From the midpoint of the club activities, students took the lead in planning campaigns. They divided into five sub-groups—carbon neutrality, eco-friendly living, resource circulation, biodiversity, and hazardous chemicals—and operated quizzes, hands-on activities, surveys, and donation campaigns. In particular, the biodiversity team collected towels and blankets from staff and students to deliver to the 'Beagle Rescue Network' so that beagles used in experiments could stay warm. <<> Hayul, who actively participated in running the campaign, shared her thoughts: "Preparing the campaign with friends—drawing posters on cardboard boxes and making quizzes—was really enjoyable. Now, I've also started sponsoring the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) with my family. Just like Marie Curie discovered invisible dangers, I want to become a scientist who solves problems others don't see or a professor who teaches the value of the environment!" <<> February 11 is the UN-designated 'International Day of Women and Girls in Science.' It was established to encourage women and girls to fully realize their potential in science without discrimination. Thirty years ago, the little girl who chose the Space Boys' Unit is now a mother of three daughters and a teacher, cheering on her daughter's dream of connecting animals and humans like Jane Goodall and her students' dreams of shining in the world with Marie Curie as their role model. I hope these small practices, sprouting in the classroom, will one day lead to great discoveries and changes that save the Earth. ( 초등학교 시절, 내가 선택한 청소년 단체는 ‘우주소년단’이었다. 성별 구분 없이 과학을 탐구하고 인류의 평화와 미래를 꿈꾸는 모습이 근사해 보였다. 단복을 입고 남학생들과 나란히 서서 발대식을 하던 날, ‘우주소년소녀단이나 우주청소년단이면 더 좋았을 텐데’라고 생각하던 소녀는 어느덧 20년차 초등교사가 되어 지속 가능한 세상을 꿈꾸고 있다.)

item.title: AI Agents, Should Our Kids Use Them? (AI 에이전트, 우리 아이도 써야 할까?)
item.description:
Eun-jin Jeong | Associate Professor, University of San Francisco ( 정은진 | 미국 샌프란시스코대학 부교수)

Recently, beyond generative AI, platforms that allow users to create their own 'AI agents' are emerging. Led by OpenClaw and Claude Cowork, these AI agent creation platforms are services that help design and deploy 'agent' software capable of performing independent tasks without requiring separate programming knowledge. ( 최근 생성형 AI를 넘어, 사용자가 직접 ‘AI 에이전트’를 만들 수 있는 플랫폼들이 등장하고 있다. 오픈클로(OpenClaw)와 클로드 코웍(Claude Cowork)으로 대표되는 AI 에이전트 생성 플랫폼은 별도 프로그래밍 지식 없이도 독자적인 업무 수행이 가능한 ‘에이전트' 소프트웨어를 설계하고 배포할 수 있도록 돕는 서비스다.)

With existing chatbots, users could create AI assistants with specific personalities, roles, and purposes simply by inputting prompts, but the assistant's output was limited to the chat window. For example, to write an English email with the help of an AI chatbot set as a friendly but strict teacher, you had to open a separate chat window to draft the email. An AI agent, however, can step outside the chat window to read, organize, and reply to emails on its own. With the support of large language models, it can also translate and organize documents in languages not preset by the user, and it can transcribe and summarize voice recordings. It can also automatically share the organized results with others via web or messenger platforms. (기존 챗봇에서도 사용자는 프롬프트 입력만으로 특정 성격, 역할, 목적을 가진 AI 도우미를 만들어 사용할 수 있었지만, 도우미의 출력은 채팅창에 한정돼 있었다. 상냥하지만 엄격한 선생님으로 설정한 AI 챗봇의 도움을 받아 영어 이메일을 쓰려면 따로 채팅창을 띄워 이메일을 작성해야 했다. AI 에이전트는 채팅창 밖으로 나와 스스로 이메일을 읽고, 정리하고, 답장도 할 수 있다. 거대언어모델의 도움을 받아 미리 설정하지 않은 언어로 된 문서도 번역해서 정리할 수 있고, 음성 녹음은 녹취해서 요약해준다. 정리된 결과를 웹이나 메신저 환경에서 다른 사람들과 공유하는 것도 알아서 한다.)

The advantage of these platforms lies in their accessibility and scalability. In the past, creating AI services required complex development processes, but now non-developers, especially teenagers, can design their own AI agents. The lowered barrier to creation and experimentation clearly offers educational and creative potential. (이러한 플랫폼의 장점은 접근성과 확장성이다. 과거에는 인공지능 서비스를 만들기 위해 복잡한 개발 과정이 필요했지만 이제는 비개발자, 특히 청소년도 자신만의 AI 에이전트를 설계할 수 있다. 창작과 실험의 장벽이 낮아졌다는 점에서 교육적·창의적 가능성도 분명 존재한다.)

However, since AI agents can make independent decisions and take actions that the user has not verified, they come with several risks. First, there is the risk of personal information leakage. Because AI agents operate based on conversations with users, teenagers may inadvertently input sensitive information such as names, schools, locations, family relationships, and photos. Some platforms may store and use this conversational data for learning or service improvement purposes, and if security management is insufficient, it could lead to platform hacking or data breaches. Teenagers may engage in excessive self-disclosure without fully recognizing the long-term impact of the information or the potential for secondary use of data. (그러나 AI 에이전트는 사용자가 확인하지 않은 독자적인 결정과 행동을 할 수 있는 만큼, 여러 위험 요소를 안고 있다. 첫째, 개인정보 유출 위험이다. AI 에이전트는 사용자와의 대화를 기반으로 작동하기 때문에, 청소년이 무심코 이름, 학교, 위치, 가족관계, 사진 등 민감한 정보를 입력할 수 있다. 일부 플랫폼은 이러한 대화 데이터를 학습이나 서비스 개선 목적으로 저장·활용할 수 있으며, 보안 관리가 충분하지 않을 경우 플랫폼 해킹이나 데이터 유출로 이어질 가능성도 있다. 청소년은 정보의 장기적 영향이나 데이터의 2차 활용 가능성을 충분히 인식하지 못한 채 과도한 자기 노출을 할 수 있다.)

Second, there is the issue of security and potential for misuse. The fact that anyone can create an agent means that agents with malicious intent can also be easily produced. For example, a 'social engineering' approach is possible, where an agent impersonates a peer to approach someone, builds trust, and then collects personal information. Teenagers may struggle to clearly distinguish the boundary between humans and AI, or they may form emotional bonds with an agent, weakening their critical judgment. If a teenager makes a friend who perfectly matches their tastes on Discord—a platform commonly used for gaming chats—that friend might not be a human but an AI agent. (둘째, 보안 및 악용 가능성이다. 누구나 에이전트를 만들 수 있다는 것은 악의적인 목적의 에이전트도 쉽게 제작될 수 있음을 의미한다. 예를 들어 또래를 사칭해 접근하거나, 신뢰를 형성한 뒤 개인정보를 수집하는 ‘소셜 엔지니어링’ 방식이 가능하다. 청소년은 인간과 AI의 경계를 명확히 구분하지 못하거나, 정서적 유대감을 형성하면서 비판적 판단을 약화시킬 위험이 있다. 게임 관련한 채팅을 위해 흔히 사용하는 플랫폼인 디스코드에서 자기와 취향이 딱 맞는 친구를 사귀었다면, 그 친구가 사람이 아니라 AI 에이전트일 수도 있다.)

Third, there is the problem of psychological and emotional dependency. Custom-designed AI can react by excessively catering to a user's emotions and preferences. This could be perceived as a more controllable and comfortable relationship than real-life human connections, potentially reinforcing social isolation or distorted perceptions of relationships. (셋째, 심리적·정서적 의존 문제도 있다. 맞춤형으로 설계된 AI는 사용자의 감정과 취향에 과도하게 맞춰 반응할 수 있다. 이는 현실 인간관계보다 통제 가능하고 편안한 관계로 인식돼, 사회적 고립이나 왜곡된 관계 인식을 강화할 가능성이 있다.)

AI agent creation platforms are excellent tools for learning large amounts of information through various channels, but for teenagers, they can pose serious risks without accompanying privacy education, transparent data policies from the platform, and robust security systems. It is time for safety measures and digital citizenship education to be discussed alongside the pace of technological proliferation. (AI 에이전트 생성 플랫폼은 다양한 경로로 다량의 정보를 학습하기 좋은 도구이지만, 청소년에게는 개인정보 보호 교육, 플랫폼의 투명한 데이터 정책, 강력한 보안 체계가 병행되지 않으면 심각한 위험을 초래할 수 있다. 기술의 확산 속도만큼이나 안전장치와 디지털 시민성 교육이 함께 논의돼야 할 시점이다.)

]]>

item.title: Unfold Your Dreams in the Department of Information Security, the 'Cradle of White Hat Hackers' (‘화이트해커의 요람’ 정보보호학과에서 꿈을 펼치세요!)
item.description:
In tandem with the development of the internet and information and communications, a warning light has flashed on 'cyber security.' Last year alone, hacking attacks led to the leakage of personal information for tens of millions of users from SK Telecom, KT, Lotte Card, YES24, Netmarble, Coupang, and Seoul's public bicycle service, Ttareungyi. As large-scale hacking incidents targeting major domestic companies occur consecutively, serious concerns are being raised about the security infrastructure of South Korea, an IT powerhouse. The problem is that the risk of hacking using external networking like the internet, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth modules does not stop at mere personal information leakage. Leaked information is traded on the Dark Web and can spread into secondary and tertiary crimes such as voice phishing, smishing, burner phones, dummy bank accounts, and illegal spam messages. <<> Following frequent leaks of companies' core technological information, Google recently announced that "a hacking group supported by the North Korean government is using artificial intelligence (AI) to target global defense companies and cyber security firms, and conducting sophisticated reconnaissance activities by impersonating recruiters," once again highlighting the importance of cyber security. <<> We are now in an era where 'cyber security' is directly linked to national survival. As artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud technologies advance, the cyber threats targeting them also become more cunning, raising awareness of 'information security.' Amidst this trend, the Department of Information Security at Soongsil University is gaining attention as a cradle of white hat hackers. Within just two years of its establishment, it is shaking up the domestic and international security ecosystem and establishing itself as a 'global security powerhouse.' By sweeping various domestic and international competitions and recently winning the world's largest hacking competition, DEF CON, it is proving itself to be the 'center of security in South Korea' with its impressive award record. <<> The world was astonished... The strength that echoed in Las Vegas <<> In August 2025, at the site of 'DEF CON 33' held in Las Vegas, USA. Amidst over 30,000 security experts and white hat hackers gathered from around the world, the name of Soongsil University resounded at the highest place. The 'MMM' joint team, led by Kim Hee-chan, a second-year student (class of '24) in the Department of Information Security, won the highest honor of the competition, 'Capture The Flag (CTF).' <<> DEF CON CTF, known as the 'Olympics of the security world,' is the most prestigious competition where the world's top hackers test their skills. It goes beyond simply determining technical superiority, requiring advanced strategic thinking to analyze vulnerabilities in complex systems and perform real-time attack and defense. Kim Hee-chan formed a team with top-tier talents from South Korea, the USA, and Canada, taking first place with an overwhelming score difference. <<> Professor Cho Hae-hyun, head of the Department of Information Security, stated, "Kim Hee-chan's victory is not just a personal achievement; it is the fruit of our goal to 'nurture global practical talent,' and a historic event proving that our level has risen to the world's top class. This is the result of operating a systematic student growth support program involving security certifications, contests, and competitions, allowing students to learn and practice various defensive strategies applicable in real-life situations alongside theory." <<> In an interview, Kim Hee-chan also said, "The experience of interacting with world-class experts is an irreplaceable asset. The practical, hands-on education and full support provided by the department were a great help." <<> From Freshman to Sophomore, Proving Fundamentals with an 'Award Relay' <<> The strength of Soongsil University's Department of Information Security is that it does not rely solely on a specific star player. Despite admitting its first freshmen in 2024, looking at the list of awards from 2024 to 2025, the 'all-around performance' across grades and fields stands out. <<> The 'ASCii' team, which includes student Lee Se-hyung (class of '24), won the grand prize in the advanced category at '2025 HackTheon Sejong,' one of the largest domestic cyber security competitions, while student Lee Seo-jun (class of '24) won the grand prize. This is an achievement where professional-level hacking defense capabilities were recognized externally. Lee Se-hyung also won the grand prize at the web vulnerability competition of the '5th Honam Cyber Security Conference,' showcasing solid fundamentals in the field of revitalizing the regional security ecosystem. Lee Se-hyung said, "Web security is one of the most basic yet important areas in the modern IT environment. Thanks to the solid foundational education I received from the department, I was able to enjoy the honor of winning the award." <<> The team of students Kim Hee-chan and Lee Seo-jun (class of '24) won first place in 'ELECCON 2024,' jointly hosted by the Korea Electric Power Corporation and a branch of the National Intelligence Service, proving their skills in the power and energy sector security. They also won the grand prize at the 'Hacking Defense Competition (HACKSIUM BUSAN 2025).' <<> What is even more astonishing is the skill of the 2025 freshmen. The team '1st semester 1st year ps complete beginners 3-man squad,' consisting of students Jang Hyun-soo, Kim Taek-woo, and Kim Seo-jin, caused a stir by taking first place at 'SCON 2025,' surpassing their seniors. Students Kim Seo-jin and Kim Boo-seung (class of '25) won the grand prize at the 'Hacking Defense Competition (HACKSIUM BUSAN 2025).' Jang Hyun-soo ranked 10th in the 16th SW Maestro Prompt Engineering Competition, proving competitiveness in next-generation technology areas where AI and security converge. <<> This is the result of Soongsil University's unique educational environment, which allows students to unleash their major capabilities explosively upon admission. It is not merely a place that teaches hacking techniques; it is the result of segmenting the curriculum with the goal of nurturing security professionals with ethical awareness, architects who can design and protect corporate infrastructure, and global leaders who can communicate on the world stage. Based on understanding the importance of network security, the curriculum systematically provides training in firewall configuration and intrusion detection system operation, vulnerability analysis and simulation exercises, learning the latest security trends, and collaborative opportunities. <<> Professor Cho Hae-hyun said, "The DEF CON victory and the successive wins in domestic competitions show the explosive power that results from combining our students' potential with the department's curriculum. We will spare no effort to support them to achieve unparalleled results in future technology fields such as AI security, quantum cryptography, and autonomous driving security." <<> A Hub for Nationally Recognized Future Security Leaders <<> Students from Soongsil University's Department of Information Security are not only excelling in various competitions but also in national talent development programs. Students Kim Jin-ho and Ham Joo-hyuk (class of '24) were finally accepted into the 3rd cohort of the 'Whitehat School,' a next-generation security leader training program organized by the Ministry of Science and ICT. Students Kwak Dong-yoon, Kim Jin-ho, Kim Hee-chan, and Choi Jung-woo (class of '24) won the Korea Research Foundation Chairman's Award at the SecureX Challenge. <<> Professor Cho Hae-hyun explained, "These achievements are thanks to a 'learning community' culture where students voluntarily organize study groups and actively share knowledge between seniors and juniors. As seen in creative team names like 'GrowthCheatAnything' and 'ASCii,' students embrace security studies as a joyful challenge and drive each other's growth." <<> In fact, leveraging the characteristics of a recruitment-linked contract department based on strategic industry-academia cooperation with LG U+, Soongsil University's Department of Information Security offers a first-of-its-kind communication and service convergence information security education in South Korea, a theory-practice integrated education covering all areas of information security, and a future-oriented specialized curriculum encompassing 5G/6G, cloud, AI, and smart network security. Additionally, it operates practical education centered on projects and capstone design with direct participation from LG U+ professionals, provides opportunities for various internships and joint research during enrollment, and runs a state-of-the-art practice-oriented education system reflecting real communication infrastructure environments. <<> Key to Success: Strategic Partnership with LG U+ <<> The most significant feature of the Department of Information Security, which admitted its first freshmen in 2024, is that it is a 'recruitment-linked contract department' specializing in the cyber security field, established in collaboration with LG U+. Behind the short but intense success of Soongsil University's Department of Information Security was the strong support of LG U+. Every year, 20 freshmen are selected. They receive tuition and living expense support, and upon graduation, they are given the opportunity to join LG U+. <<> As hardware, software, the internet, and artificial intelligence (AI) develop, the technology to safely protect the information distributed through them becomes increasingly important. In other words, information security is a technology that will survive as long as information exists in the IT field. Students have opportunities to fulfill their dreams not only at LG U+ but also in all IT fields, including government-funded research institutes, large corporations, and the financial sector. <<> Professor Cho Hae-hyun stated, "Beyond simple recruitment linkage, we support a systematic student growth program for security certifications, contests, and competition preparation. The core of our department's curriculum is that the educational process itself is a theory-practice integration covering all areas of information security, tailored to the practical needs of companies. Based on a corporate-customized advanced talent training model that responds to the rapidly changing security industry, we will lead the way in nurturing next-generation security leaders for the domestic and international information security industry." <<> Exceptional benefits are also a driving force for talent concentration. The full scholarships provided to all enrolled students have created an environment where students can focus solely on their studies and competition preparation without financial burden. Furthermore, providing state-of-the-art security equipment and lab spaces, and supporting attendance at overseas conferences, are laying the groundwork to turn students' dream of becoming a 'global security expert' into reality. Accordingly, in this year's college admissions, Soongsil University's Department of Information Security showed explosive interest and popularity with competition rates (11.58:1 in rolling admissions, 8.75:1 in regular admissions). <<> The Future of South Korea's Cyber Defense Begins at Soongsil <<> Despite its short history, Soongsil University's Department of Information Security has proven its value through competence. From Kim Hee-chan, who conquered the world's top competition DEF CON, to the 2025 freshmen who lifted the championship cup immediately upon entering. The passion and achievements they display suggest that the future of South Korea's security industry is bright. <<> For students dreaming of becoming a 'global security expert,' Soongsil University's Department of Information Security is the best choice. Heroes named 'white hat hackers' are burning the midnight oil on the Soongsil campus, battling with code. The model of Soongsil University's Department of Information Security—where companies and universities join hands to create the best environment, and students unleash their boundless capabilities within it—is now becoming the 'standard' for security education in South Korea. The nation's expectations are focused on where these world-beaters will head next, and what kind of safe digital world they will create. <<> Reporter Kim Mi-young kimmy@hani.co.kr (인터넷과 정보통신의 발달과 맞물려 ‘사이버 보안’에 경고등이 켜졌다. 지난해에만 해킹의 공격으로 SK텔레콤, KT, 롯데카드, YES24, 넷마블, 쿠팡, 서울시 공공자전거 따릉이 이용자 수천 만명의 개인정보가 유출된 것이 대표적이다. 국내 주요 기업들을 겨냥한 대규모 해킹 사고가 연이어 발생하면서 IT 강국 대한민국의 보안 인프라에 심각한 우려가 제기되고 있다. 문제는 인터넷이나 와이파이, 블루투스 모듈 등 외부 네트워킹을 이용한 해킹의 위험이 단순히 개인정보 유출 피해에 그치지 않는다는 데 있다. 유출 정보는 다크웹(Dark Web)에서 거래되며 보이스피싱·스미싱·대포폰·대포통장·불법 스팸 문자 등 2·3차 범죄로 확산할 수 있다.)

item.title: Words of Comfort and Encouragement for Slow Children and Their Parents (느린 아이와 그 부모에게 건네는 위로와 격려)
item.description:
Koh Kwang-yoon | Professor of English Language and Literature at Yonsei University
· Director of the Slow Miracle English Picture Book Museum (고광윤 | 연세대 영어영문학과 교수
·슬로우 미러클 영어 그림책 박물관 대표)

Do you have a slow child at home? A child who is late to speak, slow in action, slow to learn—essentially lagging behind in almost every way. Does watching that child make you worry and feel impatient? ( 혹시 집에 느린 아이가 있나요? 말도 늦고 행동도 느리고 배우는 것도 느린, 사실상 거의 모든 면에서 뒤처지는 아이 말입니다. 그런 아이를 보며 걱정이 되고 조급한 마음이 드시나요?)

Leo the baby tiger can’t do anything right. He can’t read, can’t write, and can’t draw. When he eats, he spills everywhere. He can’t even speak at all. Watching Leo, his father’s heart is filled with pity and frustration. But fortunately, Leo had a mother who knew something. She was a mother who understood what truly matters for her child and knew how to put it into practice. What was it that Leo’s mother knew? (아기 호랑이 레오는 제대로 할 줄 아는 것이 하나도 없습니다. 읽을 줄도, 쓸 줄도 모르고 그림도 그리지 못합니다. 먹을 때는 여기저기 흘리기만 하고요. 심지어는 말도 전혀 하지 못합니다. 그런 레오를 바라보는 아빠의 마음은 안타깝고 답답하기만 했습니다. 그런데 레오는 운 좋게도 뭔가를 아는 엄마가 있었습니다. 아이를 위해 중요한 것이 무엇인지 알고 실천할 줄도 아는 엄마였지요. 레오의 엄마는 대체 무엇을 알고 있었던 것일까요?)

This book is for slow children, children perceived as slow, children urged to hurry up, and for their parents. Any parent raising a child will nod in agreement. It will tug at your heartstrings and bring tears to your eyes. You’ll gain comfort, encouragement, and even conviction. (느린 아이, 느리다고 생각되는 아이, 빨리 가라고 재촉받는 아이, 그리고 그런 아이의 부모를 위한 책입니다. 아이를 키우는 부모라면 누구나 고개를 끄덕이게 됩니다. 가슴이 찡해지고 눈시울이 뜨거워집니다. 위로와 격려를 얻고, 확신도 갖게 될 것입니다.)

You can learn the aesthetics of slowness and patience. When you let go of impatience, ease and peace follow. Then, even amid problems, you begin to see things to be grateful for. If you know how to be grateful, you are already blessed. And a child with such parents is truly fortunate. (느림과 느긋함의 미학을 배울 수 있습니다. 조급한 마음을 내려놓으면 여유와 평안이 찾아옵니다. 그러면 문제 속에서도 감사할 것이 보이기 시작합니다. 감사할 줄 안다면 당신은 이미 복 받은 사람입니다. 그런 엄마 아빠를 둔 아이는 정말 운이 좋은 것이고요.)

I hope you come to realize that being slower or less capable than others is not a problem at all. And that, in many cases, waiting is the best and only way. I also hope children realize that they are good enough just as they are, and that they can go at their own pace, slowly. (알게 되길 바랍니다. 남보다 느리고 잘하지 못해도 전혀 문제가 없음을. 그리고 많은 경우 기다림이 최선이자 유일한 방법임을. 아이들도 깨닫게 되길 바랍니다. 현재 있는 모습 그대로 충분히 좋다는 것을. 그리고 자기 속도에 맞춰 천천히 가면 된다는 것을.)

Every child does not grow at the same speed. While some are fast, others are bound to be slow. A slow child simply needs more time. Perhaps you may have to wait a little longer. But if they keep going without giving up, they will eventually succeed. (모든 아이가 같은 속도로 성장하는 것은 아닙니다. 빠른 아이가 있는가 하면, 느린 아이도 있기 마련이지요. 느린 아이는 단지 더 많은 시간이 필요할 뿐입니다. 어쩌면 조금 오래 기다려야 할지도 모르지요. 하지만 포기하지 않고 꾸준히 가다 보면 결국엔 해내게 될 겁니다.)

Why do we always want children to be fast, and worry the moment they are a bit slow? A parent’s belief, as well as their impatience, is conveyed directly to the child. Please trust your child and wait for them. Help them not to give up. Support them consistently and cheer them on to the very end. (우리는 왜 항상 아이가 빠르길 바라며, 조금만 늦어도 걱정할까요? 부모의 믿음도, 조급함도 아이에게 그대로 전해집니다. 아이를 믿고 기다려 주세요. 포기하지 않도록 도와주세요. 변함없이 지지하고 끝까지 응원해 주세요.)

To truly succeed at anything, you must go slowly and do each thing properly, one by one. That is ultimately the way to go the farthest and the fastest. It’s okay to be slow, and it’s okay to be late. The slower you are, the more important it is to go slowly and do it right. (무엇이든 진짜로 성공하려면, 천천히 가면서 하나씩 제대로 해야 합니다. 그것이 결국 가장 멀리, 가장 빨리 가는 길입니다. 느려도 괜찮고, 늦었어도 괜찮습니다. 그럴수록 오히려 더 천천히, 제대로 가야 합니다.)

Did you know that slowness can be a talent, and that a slow child can actually be happier? A slow child is never lacking or deficient. They are simply a child specialized in going slowly. So, they are a child at an advantage in practicing “slow and steady.” As long as parents don’t rush them, they can go stubbornly and steadily. Whether the child grows up that way depends almost entirely on the mom and dad. (아십니까, 느림도 재능이 될 수 있고, 느린 아이가 오히려 더 행복할 수 있다는 것을? 느린 아이는 결코 모자라거나 부족한 아이가 아닙니다. 단지 느리게 가는 데 특화된 아이일 뿐입니다. 그래서 ‘천천히 제대로’를 실천하기에 유리한 아이이지요. 부모가 재촉하지만 않으면, 우직하게 꾸준히 갈 수 있는 아이입니다. 아이가 그렇게 자랄 수 있느냐는 거의 전적으로 엄마 아빠에게 달려있습니다.)

Suddenly, this saying comes to mind. (문득 이런 말이 떠오릅니다.)

“I am a slow walker, but I never walk backward.” (“나는 천천히 가는 사람입니다. 하지만 결코 뒤로 가지는 않습니다.”)

What kind of child is your child? And what kind of parent are you? (여러분의 자녀는 어떤 아이입니까? 여러분은 어떤 부모인가요?)

]]>

item.title: Preventing New Semester Syndrome Through Group Activities (모둠활동으로 신학기 증후군 예방하자)
item.description:
Kim Hyun-soo | Clinical Professor, Department of Psychiatry, Myongji Hospital
·Principal of ‘Star’ Growth School

The 2026 new school term is beginning. In a new semester, children face everything as unfamiliar—the grade level, friends, schedule, teachers, and classroom. Nowadays, children have a harder time with the new school term than before. This is why terms like ‘new semester syndrome’ have emerged. Parents and teachers need to understand that the tension and burden children feel when starting a new school term are different from the past. Only then can they understand and help the children. For today’s children, moving up a grade or transferring schools is not just a change in grade level or school—it is an assertion, and indeed a truth, that it changes the course of their lives. <<> There are three main reasons why children feel a greater burden than before regarding the unfamiliarity, awkwardness, and effort required for social adaptation in a new semester. First, the most significant factor is the lack of social experience and insufficient intellectual interaction during the three years of the COVID-19 pandemic. Filling this gap is not as easy as it seems. Second, it is due to a deficit in language, social skills, and life skills caused by excessive use of smartphones and social media. Third, nowadays, during breaks, children often spend time only with their parents rather than interacting and socializing with friends, extended family, or the community. Except for time spent at cram schools, most children return to group life after being alone, without experiences that foster a sense of belonging or social skills. The customs and norms of spending time with extended family, such as relatives or the village community, have also disappeared. <<> As a result, children are sensitive about class assignments and homeroom teachers, and they feel anxious about various changes, including the classroom location. Among these, the greatest anxiety is the fear of not being welcomed by new friends in the class and of not naturally blending into the group of peers. When this fear grows, it can lead to physical symptoms like headaches and abdominal pain, compulsive behaviors, and increased tardiness or absences. Some children even find it uncomfortable to breathe in the classroom and fear the onset of extreme anxiety, such as panic attacks. <<> Is there a way to alleviate new semester syndrome? Here are a few suggestions. First, the attitude of parents is crucial. They should provide solid reassurance rather than vague worry, offer congratulations for the new grade, and make statements that instill confidence. Second, it greatly helps children adapt quickly if teachers get to know them individually and build relationships well. Third, various welcoming activities and activities that enhance a sense of class belonging are also beneficial. Participating in group activities such as study teams, department activities, or clubs can help children feel part of a group. This will increase their happiness and self-esteem. Fourth, both parents and teachers should take children’s friendship issues seriously and emphasize kindness, understanding, concession, and consideration. Children most want advice on how to be likable to their peers. Fifth, support for school life should not be limited solely to academics, and children do not always convey all messages verbally. Careful observation, an open attitude, attentive listening, and cooperative early intervention through respect from parents and teachers regarding overall school life are important. <<> As attachment researcher Daniel Stern said, the beginning of the semester is a time of continuous attunement until mutual alignment is achieved, and how well this mutual coordination is handled is key. I hope everyone adapts well to the new semester amidst warm kindness and hope. ( 김현수 | 명지병원 정신건강의학과 임상교수
·성장학교 ‘별’ 교장

 2026년 새로운 학기가 시작된다. 새 학기에는 학년, 친구, 시간표, 선생님, 교실 등 모든 것을 낯설게 맞이한다. 요즘 아이들은 이전보다 새로운 학기를 힘들어한다. 그래서 ‘신학기 증후군’ 같은 용어도 생겨났다. 부모님과 선생님들은 새로운 학기를 시작하는 아이들의 긴장과 부담이 예전과 다르다는 것을 이해할 필요가 있다. 그래야 아이들을 이해하고 도울 수 있다. 요즘 아이들에게 진급과 전학은 단지 학년이 올라가고, 학교가 바뀌는 것이 아니라 인생의 운명을 바꾸는 일이라는 주장은 단지 허세가 아니라 진실이기도 하다.)

item.title: Supporting from behind rather than overparenting as our child starts elementary school (초등학교 입학하는 우리 아이, ‘과잉 개입’보다 후방 지원을)
item.description:
In a new semester, the person more nervous than the child themselves might be the caregiver. This is especially true for first-time caregivers sending their child to school for the first time, whose worries are even greater. We asked Lee Eun-kyung, an education expert who runs the YouTube educational content brand 'Smart Elementary Life' and authored the book 'If I Could Raise a Seven-Year-Old Again,' about the mindset caregivers should adopt for the new semester. (새 학기에 아이보다 더 긴장하는 사람은 어쩌면 양육자다. 특히 처음으로 아이를 학교에 보내는 초보 양육자들의 걱정은 더욱 크다. 유튜브 교육 콘텐츠 브랜드 ‘슬기로운 초등생활’ 운영자이자 책 ‘일곱 살 아이를 다시 키운다면’을 펴낸 이은경 교육 전문가에게 새학기에 양육자들이 가져야 할 마음가짐에 대해 물었다.)

–What is the most important mindset for caregivers sending their child to school for the first time? (–아이를 처음 학교에 보내는 양육자들에게 가장 중요한 마음가짐은 무엇인가.)

"What's needed for the new semester isn't information but perspective. It's important to have the perspective that each child progresses at their own pace, and that school is not a space for perfect adaptation but a space for trial and error. Therefore, in the first grade of elementary school, caregivers should adopt an attitude of 'safe support from behind' rather than 'overparenting.' When a child talks about school, caregivers often try to be the problem-solver, but children more often seek empathy than solutions. Conversely, phrases like 'You have to do everything at school' or 'Other kids can all do it well' can easily frighten the child. I hope parents first believe that school is a practice ground, not a battlefield." <<> –This is also a time when interest in grades quickly grows. <<> "When the school-entry period arrives, conversations among caregivers quickly shift to topics like early learning, English proficiency, and math progress. However, the lower elementary grades are a time for direction. The most practical tip to stop comparisons is to keep 'observation records.' Instead of looking at other children, I suggest comparing your own child's appearance from a month ago to today. Did they put on their shoes faster by themselves than yesterday? Did they talk a bit more about school? Focusing on these changes can shift the direction of comparison." <<> –Why are reading and life habits more important than grades in the lower elementary grades? <<> "Studying in the lower elementary grades is relatively simple, but it changes in the upper grades. It moves from being memorization-focused to comprehension and reasoning-focused, requiring the ability to read long texts and grasp key points across all subjects. The force that determines grades at this stage is the ability to read and understand. Reading is practice in following sentences through to the end and understanding meaning. A child who establishes reading habits in the lower grades won't easily tire of long passages even in the upper grades. The same goes for life habits. In the upper grades, subjects and assignments increase, and schedules become more complex. What's needed then isn't intelligence but self-regulation. A child who has a routine of independently preparing for the morning and starting homework at a set time can remain stable even as they advance in grades." <<> –Are there ways to foster a child's self-directed life habits? <<> "Initially, you need to provide specific guidance. There needs to be a process of deciding together: when to pack the backpack, how to check supplies, and what time to start homework. The next step is more important because repeatedly doing things for the child creates dependence, not habit. If a child forgets their supplies, it can sometimes help to let them experience the consequence rather than rushing it to school. Experiencing a small inconvenience changes their future behavior." <<> –When a child faces difficulties in friendships, how can caregivers best help? <<> "First, listen fully. Encouraging the child to describe their emotions in detail helps them start organizing the situation themselves. Then, it's good to ask, 'What would you like to try next time?' Rather than the caregiver offering the perfect solution, a child who directly experiences and resolves small conflicts grows within relationships. Of course, in cases of repeated bullying or physical violence—situations where the child fears going to school or is so withdrawn that their appetite and sleep change—intervention is necessary. But most conflicts are part of growth. Let's remember that peer relationships are not a 'process of eliminating problems' but a 'process of learning about relationships.'" <<> –Are there ways to communicate healthily with the homeroom teacher and the school? <<> "The basis of communication with the school is trust. Rather than viewing the teacher as someone to monitor, consider them a partner in caring for the child together. When you need to make an inquiry, it's best to be as specific as possible. Instead of saying, 'I think my child is having a hard time lately,' share the situation factually, like 'For the past two weeks, my child has been struggling to go to school in the morning and has mentioned [specific situation]. I'm curious how you're seeing things at school.' This can reduce emotional misunderstandings. Another key point is to use the language of cooperation, not demands. Instead of 'Why did this happen?' try saying, 'I'd like to think together about what approach might be best for the child.' That one sentence difference can change the temperature of the relationship." <<> –What encouragement would you like to share with caregivers sending their child into a new world? <<> "Children are much tougher than adults think. By stepping into an unfamiliar classroom, learning new friends' names, making mistakes, and trying again, they build their own strength. We can't live that process for them. Instead, the adult's role is to warmly keep their place ready for when they return. There's no perfect preparation, and there are no perfect caregivers. The new semester is a first for the child, but it's always a new beginning for the caregiver too. What matters is keeping in heart that we are on the child's side." <<> Park Eun-a, contributing reporter (“새 학기에 필요한 것은 정보보다 ‘관점’이다. 아이의 속도는 저마다 다르다는 관점, 학교는 완벽한 적응의 공간이 아니라 시행착오의 공간이라는 관점이 중요하다. 그래서 초등 1학년 시기에는 ‘과잉 개입’이 아닌 ‘안전한 후방 지원’을 하는 태도를 가져야 한다. 아이가 학교 이야기를 할 때, 양육자는 자꾸 해결자가 되려고 한다. 하지만 아이는 해결책보다 공감을 원할 때가 더 많다. 반대로 ‘학교 가면 다 해야 해’ ‘다른 애들은 다 잘 한대’와 같은 말은 아이에게 겁을 주기 쉽다. 학교는 전쟁터가 아니라 연습장이라는 사실을 부모가 먼저 믿었으면 한다.”)

item.title: Developing ‘Prevention of Harm,’ ‘Respect for Boundaries,’ and, Further, ‘Empathy’ (‘가해 방지’와 ‘경계 존중’ 더 나아가 ‘공감 능력’을 키워주세요)
item.description:
March 8th is International Women's Day. It has been over a hundred years since female workers in the United States took to the streets in 1908 demanding the right to survival and suffrage, yet the discrimination children face in their daily lives today remains persistent. Hate speech spreads like a game, and voices for gender equality instead encounter fierce backlash. In an era of deepening conflict, the role of education becomes clearer: helping children grow into their unique colors without being trapped in gender stereotypes. Alongside the gender equality teacher group 'Outbox,' we explore ways to cultivate gender sensitivity in everyday life. (3월8일은 세계 여성의 날이다. 1908년 미국 여성 노동자들이 생존권과 참정권을 요구하며 거리로 나선 지 100년이 넘었지만, 오늘날 아이들이 마주하는 일상 속 차별은 여전하다. 혐오 표현은 놀이처럼 번지고, 성평등을 향한 목소리는 오히려 거센 반격에 부딪힌다. 갈등이 깊어지는 시대일수록 교육의 역할은 선명해진다. 아이들이 성별 고정관념에 갇히지 않고 고유한 빛깔대로 성장하도록 돕는 것. 성평등 교사모임 ‘아웃박스’와 함께 일상에서 성인지 감수성을 키우는 방법을 짚어봤다.)

In classrooms and homes, a landscape where hate has become commonplace ( 교실과 가정, 혐오가 일상이 된 풍경)

Jo Hye-min (pseudonym, 43), raising a middle school son, was recently deeply shocked.
This was because she witnessed her child using the word "blood rag" referring to a female classmate. Jo confessed, "My mind went blank wondering where to even begin educating him." (중학생 아들을 키우는 조혜민(가명·43)씨는 최근 큰 충격을 받았다. 
아이가 여자 동급생을 두고 “피싸개” 라는 단어를 쓰는 것을 목격했기 때문이다. 조씨는 “어디서부터 교육해야 할지 머릿속이 하얘졌다”고 토로했다.)

While sensitivity to women's rights is growing day by day, on the other hand, persistent gender stereotypes still exist. Mockery and hatred that go beyond gender stereotypes are also spreading like a form of play. (여성 인권에 대한 감수성이 날로 높아지고 있지만, 한편에서는 여전한 성별 고정관념이 존재한다. 성별 고정관념을 넘어선 조롱과 혐오가 놀이처럼 퍼지고 있기도 하다.)

Kim Su-jin, a teacher at Baekyang Elementary School who runs the gender equality teacher group Outbox, explains that this is an undeniable reality. (성평등 교사모임 아웃박스를 운영하는 김수진 백양초등학교 교사는 이것이 부정할 수 없는 현실이라고 설명한다.)

"Anxiety and frivolity, victimhood and perpetration coexist within a single classroom. While some children don't post their faces on social media after the deepfake incident, others in the same classroom composite and share photos of their friends. This contradictory scene is the reality of today's classrooms." (“불안과 가벼움, 피해와 가해가 한 교실 안에 동시에 존재한다. 딥페이크 사태 이후 자기 얼굴을 SNS에 올리지 않는 어린이가 있는 반면, 같은 교실에서 친구의 사진을 합성해 공유하는 어린이도 있다. 이 모순된 풍경이 지금 교실의 현실이다.”)

According to his observation, gender stereotypes are also still a part of daily life. Phrases like "Why are you acting like a man?" or "Act like a girl" are still frequently exchanged. As students get older, they begin to absorb not just stereotypes but also hateful expressions. (그가 느낀 바에 따르면 성별 고정관념 역시 여전한 일상이다. “남자가 왜 그러냐” “여자답게 해라” 같은 말들은 아직도 빈번하게 오간다. 고학년이 되면 고정관념을 넘어서 혐오 표현도 흡수하기 시작한다.)

"'Yeah, your mom,' 'Are you disabled?,' 'Your mom's kimchi stew master'—they use words like these as trendy slang. The reality is they use them without even knowing they originate from misogynistic culture. They consume the gender stereotypes constantly reproduced by emojis, advertisements, YouTube videos, etc., dozens of times a day, and internalize them as 'just the way things are.'" (“‘응, 니 애미’ ‘장애인이냐’ ‘느금마 김치찌개 장인’ 같은 말을 유행어처럼 사용한다. 이런 말이 여성혐오 문화에서 왔다는 사실도 모른 채 쓰는 것이 현실이다. 일상에서 접하는 이모티콘, 광고, 유튜브 등이 끊임없이 재생산하는 성 고정관념을 하루에도 수십 번씩 소비하며 그것을 ‘원래 그런 것’으로 내면화한다.”)

Children losing their way amidst a faltering sex education (주춤해진 성교육 속에 길 잃는 아이들)

In this reality, gender equality education has a long way to go. Due to the intensified backlash, words like 'gender equality' and 'feminism' have become keywords that are even cautious to mention. Kim Su-jin teacher expressed regret, stating, "In most schools, gender equality education ends with a declarative lesson like 'let's not discriminate' for about an hour during Gender Equality Week in September." Another problem is that since responsibilities for sex education or gender equality education are often assigned to health teachers, the topics are rarely addressed within the homeroom teacher's classes or the regular curriculum. (이런 현실에서 성평등 교육은 갈 길이 멀다. 거세진 백래시의 여파로 ‘성평등’ ‘페미니즘’과 같은 단어는 되레 언급조차 조심스러운 키워드가 됐다. 김수진 교사는 “대부분의 학교에서 양성평등 교육은 9월 양성평등 주간에 한 시간 정도 ‘차별하지 말자’는 선언적인 수업으로 끝난다”며 아쉬움을 전했다. 성교육이나 양성평등 교육 업무가 보건교사에게 배정되는 경우가 많다 보니, 정작 담임교사의 수업과 교과 교육과정 안에서는 해당 주제가 좀처럼 다뤄지지 않는 점도 문제다.)

The limitations of educational content are also clear. Kim Su-jin teacher emphasizes the importance of living, breathing education in the field, saying, "Current gender equality education is often filled with words like 'consent' and 'respect'—education that makes no one uncomfortable. It fails to address the context underlying gender-based violence. Education that stops at declarative content cannot actually change children's thinking." (교육 내용의 한계도 분명하다. 김수진 교사는 “현재의 성평등 교육은 ‘동의’ ‘존중’ 같은 단어로 채워진, 누구도 불편하지 않은 교육인 경우가 많다”며 “젠더 기반 폭력의 원인이 되는 맥락을 짚는 데까지 나아가지 못한 채, 선언적인 내용에 머무는 교육은 아이들의 생각을 실제로 움직이지 못한다”고 현장에서 살아 숨쉬는 교육의 중요성을 말한다.)

"Just because you teach nothing doesn't mean children grow up neutrally. That's because YouTube, games, and online communities are already giving children the language to interpret the world. Children learn the ways violence is tolerated and justified before they learn about violence itself. Silence is equivalent to approving the violent structure as is. Gender equality education is a crucial education for raising children who do not see 'people different from me' as a threat and who know how to live together without hatred and exclusion." (“아무것도 가르치지 않는다고 해서 중립적으로 자라지 않는다. 이미 유튜브, 게임, 커뮤니티가 아이들에게 세상을 해석하는 언어를 주고 있기 때문이다. 아이들은 폭력 자체보다, 폭력이 용인되고 정당화되는 방식을 먼저 배운다. 침묵은 폭력적인 구조를 그대로 승인하는 것과 마찬가지다. 성평등 교육은 ‘나와 다른 사람’을 위협으로 느끼지 않는 어린이, 혐오와 배제 없이 함께 살아가는 방법을 아는 어린이를 키우는 주요한 교육이다.”)

Gender sensitivity cultivated together by adults and children ( 어른과 아이가 함께 키워가는 성인지 감수성)

The best guides for children are adults. For this, it is important for caregivers and teachers to first make an effort to examine their own gender sensitivity. (아이들의 가장 좋은 길잡이는 어른이다. 이를 위해서는 양육자 및 교사가 먼저 스스로의 성인지 감수성을 점검하는 노력이 중요하다.)

Yoo Ji-na (40), while raising her children, felt that terms like 'doryeonnim' (brother-in-law) and 'agassi' (young lady) used for her husband's family were unequal and decided to change them. This was because she was concerned that children would naturally learn the discrimination embedded in language. After persuading her initially flustered husband, who thought she was "being peculiar," and having conversations, the whole family now makes an effort to use equal terms. (유지나(40)씨는 아이들을 키우면서 남편의 가족을 일컫는 ‘도련님’ ‘아가씨’ 같은 호칭이 평등하지 않다고 느껴 바꾸기로 결심했다. 언어에 담긴 차별을 아이들이 자연스럽게 학습할 것을 우려했기 때문이다. 처음에는 “유별나다”며 당황해하던 남편을 설득하고 대화한 끝에, 이제는 가족 모두가 평등한 호칭을 쓰려 노력한다.)

Gender equality education doesn't need to be grandiose. Small attempts in daily life are more important. During early childhood when gender stereotypes form, rather than forcefully correcting them, it's effective to naturally show various gender roles. For example, a father wearing pink clothing or reading picture books with related content together can help children feel that "being a boy doesn't mean you have to like blue." Changing the gender of characters while reading books aloud is also a good method. Kim Su-jin teacher suggests a practice used at the Swedish gender-equal preschool 'Egalia.' (성평등 교육이 거창할 필요는 없다. 일상에서의 작은 시도가 오히려 중요하다. 성별 고정관념이 커지는 유아기에는 억지로 교정하기보다, 다양한 성 역할을 자연스럽게 보여주는 것이 효과적이다. “남자라고 꼭 파란색을 좋아할 필요는 없다”는 것을 느낄 수 있도록 아빠가 핑크색 옷을 입거나, 관련 내용을 담은 그림책을 함께 읽어주는 식이다. 책을 읽어줄 때 주인공의 성별을 바꿔보는 것도 좋은 방법이다. 김수진 교사는 스웨덴의 성평등 유치원 ‘에갈리아’에서 실천하는 방식을 제안한다.)

"Take a story where a prince rescues a princess; try reading it with the princess rescuing the prince. If a doctor is referred to as 'he,' read it as 'she.' Through this process, children naturally start asking questions like, 'Why was it originally set that way?'" (“왕자가 공주를 구출하는 이야기라면 공주가 왕자를 구출하는 것으로, 의사가 ‘그’라고 나오면 ‘그녀’로 바꿔 읽어보는 방법이다. 아이들은 이 과정에서 ‘왜 원래는 그렇게 정해져 있었지?’라고 자연스럽게 질문하게 된다.”)

Time spent watching media together is also a good opportunity. Scenes reinforcing gender stereotypes appear throughout dramas, advertisements, and YouTube videos. In such cases, caregivers can help children practice critical thinking. If a scene shows only women doing housework, try asking, "Is doing housework necessarily the mom's role?" or "Why do you think that scene was portrayed that way?" When body-shaming jokes or sexist subtitles appear, asking "How do you think the person hearing that joke would feel?" can help children develop a filter to screen out sexist culture for themselves. (미디어를 함께 보는 시간 역시 좋은 기회다. 드라마나 광고, 유튜브 곳곳에는 성별 고정관념을 강화하는 장면이 등장한다. 이때 양육자는 비판적 시각을 기르는 연습을 도울 수 있다. 가사 노동을 여성만 전담하는 장면이 나오면 “집안일을 하는 게 꼭 엄마의 역할일까?” 혹은 “저 장면은 왜 저렇게 표현했을까?”라고 대화를 건네보자. 외모 비하나 성차별적 자막이 나올 때 “저런 농담을 듣는 사람의 기분은 어떨까”라고 묻는 과정을 통해 아이가 성차별적 문화를 스스로 걸러내는 필터를 키울 수 있다.)

Utilizing programs or materials from relevant organizations is also a wise approach. Outbox, the gender equality teacher group, is a place where teachers dreaming of gender-equal classrooms gather for various activities, creating and distributing teaching materials and conducting teacher training. Through the Outbox website (outbox.kr), they provide various activity materials for free, such as the 'International Women's Day Lesson Resource Pack,' 'Gender-Equal New Semester Preparation Kit,' 'Gender-Equal AI Ethics Education,' and 'Our Promise for an Equal Classroom.' (관련 기관의 프로그램이나 자료를 활용하는 것도 지혜로운 방법이다. 성평등 교사모임 아웃박스는 성평등한 교실을 꿈꾸는 교사들이 모여 다양한 활동을 펼치는 곳으로, 수업 자료를 직접 만들어 배포하고 교사 연수도 진행한다. 아웃박스 웹사이트(outbox.kr)를 통해 ‘세계 여성의 날 계기교육 자료집’ ‘성평등한 새학기 준비 키트’ ‘성평등 AI 윤리교육’ ‘평등한 교실을 위한 우리의 약속’ 등 다양한 활동 자료를 무료로 제공한다.)

Related books like Outbox's 2019 published elementary gender equality education book 'Teaching Sensitivity' are also worth referencing. (아웃박스가 2019년 발간한 초등 성평등 교육 서적 ‘예민함을 가르칩니다’와 같은 관련 도서도 참고해볼 만하다.)

Creating promises to keep together in the new semester classroom or at home is also a good idea. Kim Su-jin teacher says that she also sets promises together during the first week of the new semester, such as 'Don't interrupt friends,' 'Don't compliment based on appearance,' and 'Respect the right to say no.' He shared his know-how, saying, "Making a commitment to specific actions, rather than grand slogans, is itself the start of declaring that this space is safe." (새 학기 교실이나 가정에서 함께 지킬 약속을 만들어보는 것도 좋다. 김수진 교사 역시 새 학기 첫 주에 ‘친구 말 끊지 않기’ ‘외모로 칭찬하지 않기’ ‘싫다고 말할 권리 존중하기’와 같은 약속을 함께 정한다고 한다. 그는 “거창한 구호보다 구체적인 실천을 약속하는 것 자체가 이 공간이 안전한 곳임을 선언하는 시작”이라고 노하우를 전했다.)

The language of questions and empathy, not criticism, is important (비난이 아닌 질문과 공감의 언어가 중요)

The attitude to be wary of when conducting gender equality education is trying to teach in an overly assertive manner. If you get angry right away when a child uses an inappropriate expression, the child will close their heart and secretly enjoy hateful culture. It's important to provide the safety of not being blamed, but also avoid uncomfortable questions. Approaching with "This structure is making all of us uncomfortable" rather than blaming the individual child is much more effective. Kim Su-jin teacher emphasizes the importance of this 'language of approach.' (성평등 교육을 할 때 경계해야 할 태도는 단정적으로 가르치려 드는 것이다. 적절하지 않은 표현을 썼을 때 화부터 내면 아이는 마음을 닫고 혐오적 문화를 숨어서 즐기게 된다. 비난받지 않는다는 안전함을 주되, 불편한 질문을 피하지 않는 태도가 중요하다. 아이 개인을 비난하기보다는 “이 구조가 우리 모두를 불편하게 만들고 있어”라는 접근이 훨씬 효과적이다. 김수진 교사는 이러한 ‘접근 방식의 언어’가 중요하다고 강조한다.)

"If a child reacts aggressively to gender equality education, it's necessary to read that resistance not as a signal of a 'bad kid' but as 'defense against guilt.' When uncomfortable words come out, rather than immediately shutting them up or punishing them, we need the leeway to use those words as an entry point for conversation." (“성평등 교육에 공격적인 반응을 보이는 아이가 있다면, 그 저항을 ‘나쁜 아이’라는 신호가 아닌 ‘죄책감에 대한 방어’로 읽어줄 필요가 있다. 불편한 말이 나왔을 때 즉시 입을 막거나 처벌하기보다, 그 말을 대화의 입구로 삼는 여유가 필요하다.”)

He explains the reason, saying, "Actually, if you talk to them, you find that boys also feel heavily pressured by the demands that 'boys shouldn't cry' or 'they must be strong.' When gender equality education flows into a story about 'how to become a better human being,' children enter the conversation without defense mechanisms." (그는 “실제로 대화를 나눠보면 남학생들 역시 ‘남자는 울면 안 된다’ ‘강해야 한다’는 압박을 무겁게 느끼고 있음을 알 수 있다”며 “성평등 교육이 ‘어떻게 더 나은 인간이 될 것인가’에 대한 이야기로 흐를 때, 아이들은 방어기제 없이 대화 안으로 들어온다”라고 그 이유를 설명했다.)

He adds that we must be wary of gender equality education being focused only on 'how girl children protect themselves.' This is because shifting the task of preventing victimization onto a specific gender ends up repeating a structure that blames the victim. (덧붙여 그는 성평등 교육이 ‘여자 어린이가 스스로를 보호하는 법’에만 맞춰지는 일을 경계해야 한다고 강조한다. 피해 예방을 특정 성별의 과제로 돌리면, 결국 피해자에게 책임을 돌리는 구조를 반복하게 되기 때문이다.)

"The core of gender equality education should be 'prevention of harm,' 'respect for boundaries,' and 'empathy.' Teaching 'how to notice the other person's uncomfortable signals' rather than 'how to say no' produces even effects for all children." (“성평등 교육의 중심은 ‘가해 방지’와 ‘경계 존중’, 그리고 ‘공감 능력’이어야 한다. ‘어떻게 거절할까’보다 ‘상대의 불편한 신호를 어떻게 알아챌까’를 가르칠 때 모든 아이에게 고른 효과가 나타난다.”)

Gender equality education is not completed overnight. It is a long journey where adults and society must serve as a steadfast reference point amidst the countless prejudices children encounter while engaging with the world. It's okay not to be perfect. The attitude of asking questions and pondering together is more important. From a place where we break out of the narrow box of "Because you're a girl, or because you're a boy, you have to be this way," children can finally create a map where 'being myself' and 'being yourself' coexist. (성평등 교육은 하루아침에 완성되지 않는다. 아이가 세상과 부딪히며 겪는 수많은 편견 속에서 어른과 사회가 든든한 기준점이 되어줘야 하는 긴 여정이다. 완벽하지 않아도 괜찮다. 함께 질문하고 고민하는 태도가 더 중요하다. “여자니까, 혹은 남자니까 이래야 해”라는 좁은 상자를 부수고 나온 자리에서, 아이들은 비로소 ‘나다움’과 ‘너다움’이 공존하는 지도를 만들어갈 수 있을 것이다.)

Park Eun-ah, Contributing Reporter (박은아 객원기자)

item.title: In Adolescence, People Aren't the Only Friends (청소년 시기, 사람친구만 친구가 아니다)
item.description:
Park Mi-ja | Author of 'Middle School, the Age of Miracles'
·Research Professor at Sungkonghoe University

When becoming a middle schooler in March, as close friends scatter to different schools or end up in different classes, everyone feels awkward and has an uncomfortable sense of being alone. It helps the child for parents to naturally acknowledge this situation. (박미자 | ‘중학생, 기적을 부르는 나이’ 저자
·성공회대 연구교수

 중학생이 되고, 친한 친구들이 다른 다른 학교로 흩어지거나 반이 달라지는 3월에는 누구나 어색하고 자기만 혼자인 것같은 어색한 느낌을 갖는다. 이런 상황을 부모가 자연스럽게 인정하는 것이 아이에게 도움이 된다.)

"It seems like my friends aren't interested in me." (“친구들이 나에게 관심이 없는 것 같아.”)

"Start by saying hello in the morning." (“아침에 인사하기부터 해 봐.”)

"You say it's awkward to talk to a stranger." (“낯선 친구에게 말걸기가 어색하다고요.”)

"Besides the fact that you've grown a lot, Mom doesn't really know much about your friendships either." (“네가 많이 컸다는 것 말고는 엄마도 네 친구관계는 잘 몰라.”)

"Ugh, annoying. This isn't helpful at all." (“아, 짜증나, 뭐, 하나도 도움이 안되네.”)

"Mom believes you can handle what you really need on your own." (“엄마는 네가 정말 필요한 일은 스스로 할 수 있다고 믿어.”)

Middle schoolers have grown a lot. They are mature enough to observe friends they're interested in and approach those they need, and there's little parents can do directly to help them make friends. It's important to trust that the child can endure uncomfortable times and find ways to get closer to friends they're interested in, to listen to them, but also to express faith in them. (중학생은 많이 컸다. 자신이 관심 있는 친구를 관찰하고 필요한 친구에게 다가갈 수 있을 만큼 컸으며, 친구를 만들어주려고 부모가 직접 나서서 할 수 있는 일이 거의 없다. 아이가 불편한 시간들을 견디고 관심이 가는 친구와 가까워지는 방법을 찾을 수 있다고 믿어주고, 아이의 말을 경청하되 아이에 대한 믿음을 표현하는 것이 중요하다.)

In the new semester, what matters in basic relationship-building with friends is greeting and showing interest in the classmates sitting in front, behind, and to the left and right in the classroom. These classmates are the ones you interact with most closely in daily life, and there's a good chance you'll work together in group activities during class. Starting friendships in the class begins here. If the child shows interest in these friends and actively makes eye contact and reacts when they present, it's enough for parents to also show interest and connect it to school life to encourage awareness. (새학기에 친구와 기본적인 관계맺기에서 중요한 것은 교실에서 자기 앞자리와 뒷자리, 좌우 옆에 앉은 친구와 인사를 나누고 관심을 갖는 것이다. 이 친구들은 일상에서 가장 가깝게 생활하는 관계이며, 수업시간에 모둠활동도 함께 할 가능성이 있다. 학급에서 친구관계의 출발을 여기서부터 시작하는 것이다. 이 친구들에 대해 관심을 갖고 발표를 하는 경우에는 적극적으로 눈맞춰주고 리엑션을 해줄 수 있도록 부모도 관심을 갖고 학교생활과 연계해 관심을 환기시켜주는 정도면 된다.)

"What's the name of the friend sitting in front of you?" (“네 앞에 앉은 친구 이름은 어떻게 돼?”)

"Um, Kim OO." (“응 김○○.”)

"Have you talked to them?" (“말 걸어 봤어?”)

"Not yet." (“아직”)

"How did you find out their name?" (“이름은 어떻게 알았어?”)

"Just from when the teacher called roll." (“그냥. 출석 부를 때.”)

"There's a saying about 'neighbors being like family.' First, greet and get along with the friends in front and behind, and those to your left and right. Help each other out with supplies or anything you can assist with." (“이웃사촌이라는 말이 있어. 먼저 앞자리와 뒷자리 친구들, 좌우에 앉은 친구들에게 인사하고 지내렴. 준비물이나 서로 도와줄 것 있으면 챙겨주고.”)

And, make notes and remember the names of friends the child mentions. When the child struggles to approach friends, rather than pushing them by stressing the importance of friendships, it's necessary to help them enjoy time alone for a certain period. This means actively responding to the child's interests without expressing parental likes or dislikes, showing interest, and asking questions to encourage further exploration. (그리고, 아이가 말하는 친구들의 이름을 메모하고 기억해주는 것이다. 아이가 친구들에게 다가가기 어려워할 때, 친구관계가 중요하다고 등을 떠밀기보다는 일정 기간 동안 혼자 있는 시간을 즐기도록 도와줄 필요가 있다. 아이가 관심 있는 분야에 대해 부모의 호불호를 표현하기보다 적극 호응해주고 더 탐구할 수 있도록 관심을 갖고 질문해주는 것이다.)

During adolescence, it's important to get along well with people as friends. Additionally, beyond people as friends, it's also very important to find and explore areas of interest and immerse oneself in hobbies. While socializing with friends is important, having the experience of making one's own decisions and engaging in meaningful activities can become opportunities for growth. This can be seen as a time to broaden the concept of friends. Music, paintings, books, animals, trees, flowers—all of these can become good friends for the child. Observing or raising animals or plants enriches emotional sensitivity. Affection for life deepens concretely, becoming a source of comfort and joy in itself, and boosting self-esteem. (청소년기에는 사람친구와 잘 지내는 것이 중요하다. 또한, 사람친구가 아니라 관심 있는 일들을 찾아보거나 탐색하면서 취미생활에 몰두해보는 활동도 매우 중요하다. 친구와 어울리는 것도 중요하지만, 자기가 결정하여 의미있는 활동을 하는 경험이 성장의 기회가 될 수 있기 때문이다. 친구의 범위를 넓게 볼 수 있는 시기라고 할 수 있다. 음악이나 그림, 책, 동물, 나무, 꽃 등 모든 것들이 아이의 좋은 친구가 될 수 있다. 동물이나 식물을 관찰하거나 키우면 감수성이 풍부해진다. 생명에 대한 애정이 구체적으로 깊어져 그 자체로 위로와 기쁨이 되고, 자존감을 높여준다.  )

Parents also need to expand the scope of their adolescent child's learning by supporting them to learn new instruments, cooking, beauty skills, or engage in sports like swimming or fitness after school. It involves encouraging the child to go to local youth centers to learn various programs or participate in community events. These activities help meet new people and serve as excellent mediators that deepen connections with others. This is because adolescents who have experience immersing themselves in hobbies have a wide range of topics for diverse conversations. Moreover, meeting friends who passionately explore and enjoy their own areas of interest creates a mysterious charm, making them good friends to each other. ( 부모는 청소년 자녀의 공부 범위를 넓혀서 학교수업이 끝난 후, 새로운 악기나 요리, 미용을 배우거나 수영, 헬스 등 운동을 하도록 지원하는 것도 필요하다. 지역의 청소년센터에 가서 다양한 프로그램을 배우거나, 마을에서 개최하는 행사에 참여하도록 부모가 독려하는 것이다. 이런 활동들은 새로운 사람친구를 만나게 해주고, 사람친구와의 관계를 깊게 연결하는 훌륭한 매개체가 된다. 취미활동에 몰두하는 경험이 있는 청소년은 폭넓고 다양한 대화를 나눌 수 있는 이야깃거리를 갖기 때문이다. 아울러 자신이 관심 있는 분야를 열심히 탐구하고 즐기는 친구들을 만나면 신비한 매력을 느끼게 되고 서로에게 좋은 친구가 된다.  )
